title: Creation begins
hookLine: by His will the play begins (Sukhmani 21)

cards: A blank document, and a cursor blinking. Blink. Blink.

Anyone who has had to write something knows that cursor. Everything you could say is still possible, and nothing has been said. Then you type the first word, and suddenly there's a direction, a voice, a shape.
The page will never be blank in quite the same way again. After two days of stillness, the twenty-first ashtpadi reaches its first word.

teach.b: The stanzas of the twenty-first ashtpadi keep asking what was there before, and then, near the end, the scene changes.

In paraphrase: when He Himself fashioned the world of forms, He spread it out through the three qualities; then sin and virtue came to be spoken of, some went to hell and some longed for heaven. Here's the shape of it.
First the stillness, sunn. Then, by God's own choice, forms. Only then everything that fills our lives: right and wrong, reward and loss, hope and fear.

teach.h: RIGHT AND WRONG ARRIVE WITH THE WORLD.
teach.b: They arrive with the world, not before it. The three qualities, the trigun, are an old Indian idea that Gurbani uses often: everything made is woven from three strands, roughly calm, restless and heavy.
Gurbani treats them as part of the made world, which God stands beyond. What sets it all going?
Sikh teaching answers with one word: hukam, God's will or order. In Japji, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: by His hukam forms are created; the hukam can't be described.

teach.h: KHEL: MADE FREELY, LIKE A PLAY.
teach.b: And the picture Sukhmani keeps returning to is a play, khel. God sets His own khel in motion, and is in it. That word matters.
A play isn't a machine, ground out because it must be. It's made freely, with delight. Sikh teaching doesn't say why God began the play, beyond that it was God's will.
It leaves the why with the One who began it.

how: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib's twenty-first ashtpadi hear creation begin by God's hukam, as God's own play, after the stillness of sunn.

o: play: the world made freely, with delight
a machine that runs by itself, by force
a show staged to trick the people watching

p: the three qualities of the made world

s: in Sukhmani, right and wrong existed before the world
they come to be spoken of only once forms are made.
Sukhmani pictures creation as God's own play
khel: something made freely, which God is in.
Gurbani explains exactly why God began creating
it says it was God's will, hukam, and leaves the why with God.

games.q: the stillness of sunn gives way to a world. by Sukhmani and Japji, what sets it going?
games.why: hukam. Japji says forms are made by His hukam, and the hukam can't be described. Sukhmani calls the result God's own khel, play.

practice: Sit for a moment in stillness, the way the ashtpadi did.

Then make one tiny beginning right where you are, the first sentence of a letter, one line in a notebook, the first step of a recipe, and notice the shift from nothing to something, without needing to know the ending.
If you pray, begin with Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Khel, play or game: by God's hukam the stillness gives way to forms, and the world, with all its right and wrong, starts as God's own khel.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: khel, play or game; Gurbani calls creation God's own khel.

carryVoice: Your line: the play begins. Made freely, the way a play is. Day five hundred twenty, done.
